_README: The CLOSED set of paths a release may contain that are not tracked at the deployed commit.
Anything else stops the deploy before the symlink switch. Recording an unexplained path in a
receipt was rejected as insufficient: an auditable record of contamination is not an identity
proof, and the three paths measured in production release 20260824_134957 -- two untracked
documents and one gitignored .pyc -- had shipped for weeks without anyone noticing.
Every field is required and the schema is closed: an unknown field, kind or scope is refused by
scripts/lib/release-export.sh rather than ignored. `scope` is `path` for a single entry and `tree`
for an entry that permits everything beneath it.
An entry is a PERMISSION, not a requirement: a listed path that is absent is not an error, which
is what lets this fixture describe a release built before an addition existed. Removing an entry
makes the path unexplained, so a stale fixture fails loudly instead of widening silently.
RELEASE_RECEIPT.json was deliberately ABSENT until P1.4c was reviewed. That guard did its job: the
first attempt to implement P1.4c was stopped by this gate, which refused to publish a release
carrying an unreviewed path, and the entry below was added under explicit authorization rather
than by widening the set to make an increment fit.

entries.detail: Shared environment, persistent across releases. Judged as a symlink and never followed: no line of it is read, hashed or recorded by the export gate.

Shared environment. Also the source of NEXT_PUBLIC_ENABLE_HATE_CRIME, which the build bakes into the client bundle -- which is why the same commit can produce different artifacts, and why P1.4c binds the NEXT_PUBLIC_ set as a closed build input.
RTCI and Historical data, shared and mutable. The link exists so fallback paths relative to cwd resolve. Never followed.
Query log, shared and mutable. Never followed.

entries.produced_by: scripts/deploy-zero-downtime.sh writes it before the build
entries.detail: Seven lines of provenance, stamped BEFORE npm run build so an aborted build still leaves an identifiable directory. That ordering is also why it structurally cannot carry any digest of the build output, and why P1.4c adds a separate post-build receipt rather than extending this file.

entries.produced_by: scripts/generate-release-receipt.js, run from the exported release after npm run build and before publication
entries.detail: The artifact receipt: commit and tree, the locks, the build toolchain, the CI pins, the closed NEXT_PUBLIC_ build inputs, and the manifest digest over every behaviour-bearing byte including node_modules. It exists as a second, post-build file because RELEASE_INFO is stamped BEFORE the build -- so an aborted build still leaves an identifiable directory -- and therefore structurally cannot carry a digest of the build output. Reviewed and authorized as part of P1.4c.

Generated by Next during the build and gitignored, so it is absent from the commit tree. Measured present in release 20260824_134957 and absent from the operations repo worktree listing, which is how it was identified as build output rather than a copied file.
599 files and 79.6 MB in release 20260824_134957. Permitted as a whole tree here; P1.4c digests its behaviour-bearing contents and excludes only cache, trace, trace-build and diagnostics.

26,798 files in release 20260824_134957, including the native better_sqlite3.node and next-swc modules that the workers memory-map. Permitted as a whole tree here; P1.4c digests it, because excluding it would exclude the only native code in the process.
